name: IJN Chikuma
shortDescription: The Japanese cruiser line's starter ship: eight guns, tough plating, and real speed for tier I, at the cost of turning like a barge.

turrets.note: Casemate mount, fixed to this broadside only.

consumables.name: Damage Control Party
consumables.flavor: 5s action, 60s cooldown, unlimited charges. Same fast reset every tier I cruiser starts with, nothing unique to this hull.

strengths: Eight 152mm guns is more barrels than almost anything else at tier I, Albany included
13,100 hull HP and armor up to 102mm shrug off small-caliber fire better than a light cruiser has any right to
26-knot top speed and a 3.8s rudder shift let her dictate range instead of just absorbing it
9.1 km gun range already reaches out further than Albany's before any upgrades are in play
weaknesses: 530m turning radius is wide for the tier, she doesn't jink or reposition tightly once committed
12s reload on all eight guns means that firepower advantage comes out in a slow drip, not a burst
No self-heal, Damage Control Party only resets fire and flooding
Engine and steering spaces are easy to knock out, a disabled ship can't use the speed that's her main edge
tips: Use the speed to pick your range and hold it, this ship's real strength is dictating the engagement, not brawling
Don't try to out-turn anything, that wide turning radius will get you caught broadside
Keep firing angles open early since the reload is slow, a missed salvo costs you more than it does on faster-firing peers
Watch your engine rooms against anything that can disable you, losing that speed edge undoes most of what this ship is good at

threats.threat: Anything that can cripple her engine or steering
threats.reason: Speed and rudder response are her main tools, and both disappear the moment either module goes down.

threats.threat: Ships that can out-turn her in a close brawl
threats.reason: 530m turning radius means she can't out-maneuver a fight she didn't choose the range for.

summary: Eight-gun starter cruiser built around speed and raw gun count rather than agility.
Tougher than a typical tier I hull, with armor and hit points that absorb small-caliber fire well.
Turns wide and reloads slow, so she wins by controlling range, not by out-maneuvering anyone.
playstyle.detail: Chikuma sets the tone for the whole Japanese cruiser line: more guns than the tier expects, real speed to back it up, and a hull that can take a hit. The tradeoff is a turning circle that feels more like a small battleship than a cruiser, so she's not built for close-range dogfighting. Use the speed to open the range you want, keep that eight-gun broadside working steadily against the slow reload, and don't get lured into a turning fight you can't win.
